name: Murfreesboro
seed: One of the fastest growing cities in Tennessee, with many newer subdivisions that have HOA rules. The Stones River runs through town and the Stones River National Battlefield sits on the north side. Limestone sits close to the surface in much of Rutherford County, and cedar glades are part of the landscape, so post holes can hit rock.

name: Smyrna
seed: Home to the Nissan Smyrna assembly plant, so many households work shifts. Percy Priest Lake is close to the north and east side of town. Lots of subdivisions built in the last twenty years, many with HOA review.

name: La Vergne
seed: Sits on I 24 between Nashville and Murfreesboro, with Percy Priest Lake along its northern edge. A mix of starter homes, rentals, and newer builds, so budget minded projects and rental property work are common.

name: Eagleville
seed: A small rural town in the southwest corner of Rutherford County. Bigger lots, pasture, and acreage, so long fence runs, gates wide enough for equipment, and fencing around animals come up more than in town.

name: Nashville
seed: Older neighborhoods with small lots, alleys, and houses close together, where privacy from neighbors is the main reason people call. Some neighborhoods sit inside historic or conservation zoning overlays that review exterior changes. Permits run through the Metro government's codes office.

name: Brentwood
seed: Larger lots, wooded hills, and established subdivisions where HOA architectural review is common and homeowners expect a high finish level. Sloped backyards often mean raised decks and stepped fence lines.

name: Franklin
seed: A historic downtown where exterior changes in the historic district go through design review, plus planned communities like Westhaven and Berry Farms with their own design standards. The Harpeth River winds through the area.

name: Spring Hill
seed: Grew fast around the General Motors plant, with the city spread across Maury and Williamson counties. Mostly newer subdivisions with HOA rules on fence style and height, and many young families who want fenced yards for kids and dogs.

name: Columbia
seed: The Maury County seat, with a historic downtown square and older homes on established lots, plus newer growth on the edges. The Duck River runs along the north side of town. Older houses often need a deck replaced rather than patched.

name: Hendersonville
seed: Sits on Old Hickory Lake, so lake lots, views worth keeping, and slopes down to the water are common. Shoreline work on the lake falls under the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, separate from the city.

name: Gallatin
seed: The Sumner County seat, with a historic downtown, lake communities on Old Hickory Lake, and new subdivisions spreading out from town. Golf course and lake lots bring their own HOA rules.

name: Goodlettsville
seed: A city that sits across the Davidson and Sumner county line near the Rivergate area, with older ranch homes on established lots next to newer builds. Many older decks here are due for replacement.

name: Mount Juliet
seed: Rapid growth with many new subdivisions and HOA rules, and Old Hickory Lake along the north side of town. New build yards often come with no fence at all and a builder grade deck or small patio.

name: Lebanon
seed: The Wilson County seat, near Cedars of Lebanon State Park and its cedar glades, where soil is thin over limestone. A mix of in town lots and acreage outside town with barns, animals, and long fence lines.

name: Shelbyville
seed: Known for the Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration and horse farms in the surrounding county, with the Duck River running through town. Farm and pasture fencing sits alongside in town privacy fences.

name: Manchester
seed: Home to Old Stone Fort State Archaeological Park and the rivers that meet there. Rural and small town lots, many on acreage, where long fence runs and freestanding decks are common.

name: McMinnville
seed: Known as the Nursery Capital of the World for its many plant nurseries, near the foot of the Cumberland Plateau. Rolling ground and larger lots, where homeowners often want fences that keep deer out of gardens.

name: Smithville
seed: The DeKalb County seat, close to Center Hill Lake, where lake homes sit on steep, wooded lots. Decks here are often tall and built to take in the water view. Center Hill Lake is managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

name: Cookeville
seed: The largest city in the Upper Cumberland and home to Tennessee Tech, so rental property near campus is common. Rolling hills on the edge of the Cumberland Plateau mean many sloped yards.

name: Baxter
seed: A small town just west of Cookeville, with rural lots, pasture, and homes along the Falling Water River. Long fence lines, gates for equipment, and simple, sturdy decks are the usual requests.
